experiments.question: Does doubling a binding physical limit raise living standards?
experiments.ruleChanged: The hot spring’s warm ponds are fixed by nature and bind every day: 2 sites (base) vs 4 (changed).
experiments.claim: Doubling the binding physical limit raises living standards: more of the good, a higher mean living standard and a higher one for the poorest decile.
experiments.evidence: spring 1.20 → 2.00 h a person a day (badge “nature” on 100.0 % of base days), mean 56.56 → 57.42, poorest decile 26.05 → 27.17; physics ceiling 61.88 → 63.09
experiments.takeaway: Doubling the warm ponds took spring time from 1.20 to 2.00 hours a person a day, and its price from 0.12 to 0.04 R. The mean living standard went from 56.56 to 57.42 (1.5 %), the poorest decile’s from 26.05 to 27.17.

experiments.question: Through a drought, a dark winter, two failing COOPs and a failing well, does everyone keep the basics, and does every decile recover within two years?
experiments.ruleChanged: No shocks (base) vs five scheduled shocks (changed): a drought (rain −50 %, summer of year 2), a dark winter (sun −60 %, winter of year 3), two COOPs’ output to 10 % for a year (HOME-B, a bed COOP, and GOODS-A, year 5), and the geothermal well down for 90 days (winter of year 6).
experiments.claim: Nobody is short in any shock, and every decile is back within two years (P3 holds with the shocks excused for two years).
experiments.evidence: short 6,100 person-days ({"water: energy":30,"energy: energy":61,"bed: energy":61}); P3 fails (worst fall outside the windows 7.8 %; failing: holdings decile 1, holdings decile 2, holdings decile 3, holdings decile 4, holdings decile 5, aven decile 1, aven decile 2, aven decile 3, aven decile 4, aven decile 5)
experiments.takeaway: Through the shocks, 6,100 person-days were short of a basic (0 without shocks). The largest fall of any decile outside the two-year recovery windows was 7.8 % (1.7 % without). The mean living standard ended at 57.39 vs 58.71. There were 9 receiverships vs 9.

scenarios.name: prop3-headline
scenarios.claim: On every seed: nobody below 98 % of a basic after day 0; the owner-only cohort passes the strict test by day 120 and the normal test every day; every decile (by holdings and by Aven output) never falls more than 2 % in a 5-year window and rises or sits near the physics ceiling; MIND never binds a basic.
scenarios.takeaway: Proposition 3 holds on 5 of 5 seeds over 30 years. The strict test holds from day 9 at the latest. The worst 5-year fall of any decile is 1.68 %.
scenarios.evidence: seed 20261012: P1 0 person-days short, strict from day 9, normal pass, P3 pass, worst fall 1.68 %, MIND binds a basic on 0 days; seed 1: P1 0 person-days short, strict from day 9, normal pass, P3 pass, worst fall 0.88 %, MIND binds a basic on 0 days; seed 2: P1 0 person-days short, strict from day 9, normal pass, P3 pass, worst fall 1.33 %, MIND binds a basic on 0 days; seed 3: P1 0 person-days short, strict from day 9, normal pass, P3 pass, worst fall 1.19 %, MIND binds a basic on 0 days; seed 4: P1 0 person-days short, strict from day 9, normal pass, P3 pass, worst fall 1.16 %, MIND binds a basic on 0 days. The world model asks for 60 years; this suite runs 30.

scenarios.name: melt-idle
scenarios.claim: One global melt index: 100 idle MIND keep 49.66 after 10 years; the half-life is 9.90 years; the engine’s index matches e^(−0.07 t) to within 1e-9.
scenarios.takeaway: After 30 years the melt index is 0.122456, as e^(−0.07 t) says. 100 idle MIND keep 49.66 after 10 years. The half-life is 9.90 years.
scenarios.evidence: relative error 5.1e-15

scenarios.name: steady-state
scenarios.claim: Money a person follows u/r · (1 − e^(−r t)) exactly (every HEART makes one MIND, everything melts), toward m* = u/r ≈ 125,143.
scenarios.takeaway: After 30 years a person’s share of all MIND is 109,829, 87.8 % of the resting level 125,155. It matches the closed form to 6.7e-16.
scenarios.evidence: count 109,829 vs formula 109,829; m* 125,155 vs the paper’s 125,143

scenarios.name: main-round-trip (30-year part)
scenarios.claim: People own at least 90 % of all MIND (the paper: 94 %). Issued and melted R a person a day are reported (at rest they meet; 30 years is not yet rest).
scenarios.takeaway: People own 90.3 % of all MIND after 30 years; treasuries 3.8 %, pools 5.9 %. In year 30, 24.01 R a person a day was issued and 21.00 R melted.
scenarios.evidence: holdings Gini 0.40

scenarios.name: hoard vs payout
scenarios.claim: With treasuries keeping their surplus, people hold far less of all MIND: a gap of at least 50 points (the paper: 94 % vs 30 %).
scenarios.takeaway: With payout, people hold 90.3 % of all MIND; when treasuries keep their surplus, 51.1 %. The poorest decile lives at 33.15 vs 13.90.
scenarios.evidence: gap 39.3 %; keep world: P1 pass, P2 pass, P3 fail

scenarios.name: law5-ladder
scenarios.claim: Law 5 shares of 20, 35 and 50 %: the dividend yield on people’s holdings (μ) stays below the 7 % melt in every year after year 2, and Proposition 3 holds at each share.
scenarios.takeaway: At 20 %, the yield was 30.3 % in year 1 and 1.3 % in year 30. It stayed under 7 % from year 5. At 35 %, the yield was 53.5 % in year 1 and 2.6 % in year 30. It stayed under 7 % from year 9. At 50 %, the yield was 76.2 % in year 1 and 4.7 % in year 30. It stayed under 7 % from year 15. The strict test held from day 9, 9, 27.
scenarios.evidence: 20 %: max yield after year 2 12.25 %, Prop 3 pass, poorest holdings decile 33.15; 35 %: max yield after year 2 23.88 %, Prop 3 pass, poorest holdings decile 29.23; 50 %: max yield after year 2 41.18 %, Prop 3 fail, poorest holdings decile 25.05
